articles.title: What Does It Mean to Age Well? Three Experts Weigh In
articles.summary: When people tell Dr. Dean Ornish they want to live longer, he asks them why. Maybe they want to dance at their kid’s wedding, they say, or finally write the book they’ve been thinking about for years. Whatever their answer, it gives them something to work toward and can make changing a habit today feel worth the effort. articles.title: Why the BAAJA Permitting Reform Bill Is Dividing Climate and Energy Advocates
articles.summary: The Senate voted on Nov. 18 to move forward with the Bipartisan Affordability and American Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026, a controversial permitting reform bill that aims to speed up the nation’s ability to build infrastructure and energy —which can often take years under the current process. The bill—which has divided environmentalists and clean energy advocates—will now face a final Senate vote before moving to the House of Representatives. articles.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth May Be Less a Film than a Vibe
articles.summary: It’s easy to feel nostalgia for the Hollywood filmmaking of the 1970s, when wily young directors succeeded in shaking the big-studio money tree to fund their outlandish, and often brilliant, projects. But we’ve also reached the era where the movies of the 1990s look pretty damn good. Which means David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is probably hitting at the right time.
